transportFormDiagnostic.target: Public Google API service root, no key, body or model generation.
transportFormDiagnostic.conclusion: Plain curl with a static configuration reached the public host; shell process substitution failed host resolution in this environment.
transportFormDiagnostic.limit: These observations identify a command-form difference; they do not identify the underlying sandbox implementation or prove authenticated provider operation.

workflow: Validate the claimed request using the unchanged v2 guard in a local helper.
Write the validated configuration exclusively to a mode 0600 file inside a mode 0700 directory.
Return only safe JSON metadata and the private static path.
The dispatcher may invoke the separately permitted plain curl command with that path; the wrapper itself performs no networking.
timingMeaning: Pre-tool validation and configuration preparation, not actual network start. The external tool scheduling gap remains after preparation.

safety.pacingMeaning: Retains the existing coordinator/preparation-time pacing and rate settings. Actual network-start times are unobserved; delayed external launches can compress actual start gaps, so this is not proof of at least 4,500 ms between network starts.

offlineVerification.fileOnlyParseDescription: A temporary generated test configuration is converted to file:///dev/null and written mode 0600 in a mode 0700 directory. The exact write-out framing is preserved. Real plain curl -fsSL --config with that static filename parses it successfully; one file URL and proto = file are asserted.
coverage: Private static output and unchanged validated contents.
Expiry before or immediately after validation creates timeout completion but no URL config.
Existing receipt/config prevents replay or overwrite.
Owner mismatch, changed guard bytes and unsafe config directory fail closed.
Actual queue generator and file-only curl parsing.

limitations: This wrapper restores the permitted ordinary curl command form; it does not eliminate tool-orchestration suspension.
A late external tool start can still outlive the absolute caller deadline even though relative max-time was computed before submission.
Original v2 launch receipt field names describe local preparation in this mode; the explicit pre-tool receipt supplies the correct interpretation.
The operator must record the wrapper and command form in any separately reviewed continuation permit under existing user authorization.
Existing pacing is measured at local configuration preparation, not actual network start. The wrapper does not establish a minimum actual network-start interval.

independentReview.scope: Reviewed the private wrapper and repeated its offline suite. The file-only curl test used the same plain static-filename command form. This does not establish provider availability or actual network-start timing.
